explanation: Trochozoans also include Molluscs and Annelids. Molluscs (Mollusca) have a developed three-part body plan. They include: Bivalves (Bivalvia), which have a two-part shell (clams, scallops, mussels); Gastropods (meaning 'stomach foot'), which have a long, flattened foot and often a coiled shell (snails, slugs, conch, nudibranchs); and Cephalopods (meaning 'head foot'), which have well-developed brains (squid, octopus). Annelids (Annelida) are segmented worms with a repeating body segment pattern and a closed circulatory system; examples include earthworms, marine worms, and leeches.
